<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9040945d09154481565b9992b07e83273a0fb61e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Security review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee089fe5e49e7b0ba87c5c197d0ef3f418383acc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: card #24137 (body and all 11 comments: triage bound `6229381872`, ruling `6232069920`, split `6232498969`, spec review notes `6237306208`, #24166 dev notes `6240513333`, dev report `6243083647`); PR #24229 body, file list and net diff `origin/main...ee089fe5e` (5 files, +440/-9); PR #24189 and PR #24218 bodies and file lists; on the head: `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.oauth-organization.test.ts`, `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`, `.changeset/24137-oauth-token-organization.md`; on `origin/main` (`d3d064447`): `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` (the API-key arm, the session arm at `:543`-`:566`, the #15409 block at `:712`-`:732`, `vetOrganizationClaim` `:768`-`:776`, `grantAppliesInTenant` `:861`, `resolveUserAuthzGrants`), `packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/admission-tenancy-posture.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts` (`effectiveTenancyPosture`), `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` (`consentOrganizationOf`, the `oauthProvider` options, `verifyMcpAccessToken`), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts` (`buildContextForUser`, `resolveDelegatorContext`), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/managed-object-write-denies.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-resource.object.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts` (the `/mcp` door, the environment-membership gate, `resolveActiveOrganizationId`), `packages/runtime/src/api-exposure.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/security/security-catalog.testkit.ts`; the lockfile-pinned `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.3` dist (`introspect-CbhhXT0E.mjs` `resolveAccessTokenClaims`, `getResourceCustomClaims`, `RESERVED_ACCESS_TOKEN_CLAIMS`; `authorize-9whjxVLJ.mjs` the `/admin/oauth2/resources` endpoints and `assertResourcePrivileges`), read from a sibling worktree's `node_modules`; the 38 check-runs on the head.

### ① Boundary

**Before.** `getSessionForProvenance` answered `{ user: { id } }`. The session arm read `session.activeOrganizationId` as `undefined`, so `tenantId` stayed unset, `resolveUserAuthzGrants` kept only global rows (`grantAppliesInTenant`: `!organizationId || organizationId === tenantId`), and `resolveDelegatorContext` resolved the D10 delegator with `liveTenantId` undefined. An ordinary user's agent held nothing; a platform admin's agent held its global grant and, under `isolated`, was walled to `RLS_DENY_FILTER` on every business object.

**After.** The synthetic session carries `session.activeOrganizationId = verified.organizationId`, and nothing else changes in the path. Traced on `origin/main`:

1. `resolveAuthzContextInScope` `:550` takes `tenantId ?? sessionData.session.activeOrganizationId`. The synthetic getter ignores its `headers` argument, so the only input is the verifier's result; no header, cookie or request parameter reaches it.
2. `:601` resolves grants IN that tenant; `:712`-`:732` vets the claim against the `sys_member` rows just read (`vetOrganizationClaim`), drops it under `isolated`/`group` when no current membership backs it, warns, and RE-resolves with no tenant (so `org_user_ids` is recomputed too). Under `single` or with no posture the rule returns the claim unread, as it does for a browser session.
3. The envelope's `tenantId` is `authz.tenantId`, the vetted value (`assembleExecutionContext` `entryFields`); `isSystem` is hard-coded `false`; `principalKind` is `'agent'` only when `azp` is present and the delegator is `authz.userId`.
4. The D10 middleware calls `resolveDelegatorContext(ql, context)`, which reads `context.tenantId` and resolves the delegator's grants in that organization only; `accessible_org_ids` is the delegator's own memberships, never inherited.

**Measured against the ruling's text.** One organization, the consent-bound one: yes, the claim is the consent's `reference_id` minted by `customAccessTokenClaims`, and a refresh carries the family's own reference, never the session's (PR #24218, pinned there). Re-checked every request through the existing session path: yes, the #15409 block runs on every request. Never the union: the grant resolution is `grantAppliesInTenant` against one `tenantId`. Never the browser session's current organization: the dispatcher's only raw session read (`http-dispatcher.ts` `:1657`-`:1690`, the environment-membership gate) uses the cookie session, which an OAuth-only request does not carry, and `resolveActiveOrganizationId` reads the vetted `executionContext.tenantId`. Never a widened global grant: no global row is added anywhere. Gone membership: dropped under a wall, re-resolved with no organization. No claim: `activeOrganizationId: undefined`, byte-for-byte today's resolution.

**Places the token could act elsewhere or keep acting, each judged:**

- *`group` posture read reach.* `vetOrganizationClaim` keeps the claim while the user is a member, grants are resolved in the bound organization, but Layer 0 under `group` is `organization_id IN accessible_org_ids` (`tenant-layer.ts` `:143`-`:151`) for EVERY principal, the delegator's own membership set included. A token bound to `org_alpha` for a user who is also in `org_beta` therefore reads `org_beta` rows under `group`, with `org_alpha`'s grants. That is ADR-0105 D2's design for the same user's browser session, parity is pinned at the resolver level, and the PR body names the middleware half as unmeasured. It is the session path the ruling asked for, not a widening by this diff. Observation.
- *`single` and no-posture membership loss.* The claim stands unread, so a former member's token keeps acting in the bound organization with whatever grant rows survive the membership's end (the `u_ex` fixture shape: a `sys_user_position` row in `org_alpha`, no `sys_member` row). The ruling's item 3 says the token "falls back to no organization" and item 2 fixes the mechanism as "the existing session path"; under `single` that path has no wall, so item 3's fall-back is the walled postures' behaviour. The same user's session behaves identically there (pinned: `BOUNDARY` under `single`, and the four-posture parity case), and the docs, the changeset and the PR body all state the qualifier. Within the ruling; the seat should be aware the open-core default does not re-check membership for tokens any more than it does for sessions.
- *Unusable engine.* `:591` returns the context with the unvetted `tenantId` and empty grants when `ql.find` is not a function. Pre-existing for sessions; with no grants on either leg the D10 intersection admits nothing. Not a widening.
- *API key beside a JWT bearer.* Step 1 admits the key first, sets `userId`, and the session arm is skipped, so the token's `organizationId` is never read; the key's own vetted organization governs. The pre-existing cross-credential composition (agent ceiling from the token's scopes, delegator from the key's owner) is untouched by this diff and outside its scope. Not a widening.
- *Writing the organization from the request.* `consentOrganizationOf` reads the session the provider hands it and nothing else; the client's `organization_id`-shaped authorize parameters change nothing (pinned in PR #24218). The verifier refuses a present-but-malformed claim. Unreachable.

### ② Attack paths

**(a) An `organization_id` the user did not consent to, via `sys_oauth_resource.custom_claims`.** The provider merges `extensionClaims`, then `perRequestClaims`, then the plugin's `customAccessTokenClaims`, then `resourcePolicyClaims` (`resolveAccessTokenClaims`, `introspect-CbhhXT0E.mjs` `:239`-`:262`), and `resourcePolicyClaims` come from the live `oauthResource` rows (`getResourceCustomClaims` `:591`-`:607`). `organization_id` is not in `RESERVED_ACCESS_TOKEN_CLAIMS`, so a row's value does replace the consent's on every MCP token. Who can write that row: the REST data door is closed for every verb (`sys-oauth-resource.object.ts` `:167` `apiMethods: []`, which `resolveEffectiveApiMethods` resolves to deny-all, `api-derivation.ts` `:301`, answered 405 by `checkApiExposure`; the platform admin's wildcard does not reopen it); the MCP data bridge runs the same `checkApiExposure` gate through `callData`; the provider's own `PATCH /admin/oauth2/resources/:identifier` is `SERVER_ONLY` (in-process `auth.api` only, and plugin-auth passes no `resourcePrivileges`); every default write-granting set carries a deny on `managedBy: 'better-auth'` objects. What remains is an operator with store access or in-process code. If such an operator writes it: under `isolated`/`group` the runtime keeps the override only when the user is a current member there (then the token acts there, indistinguishable from consent) and drops it otherwise (pinned, H4 `org_gamma`); under `single` or no posture it stands as a session's claim would, which retargets only which organization's grant rows apply, with no wall to cross. **Unreachable from any public door; bounded by the vetting under a wall; the residue is an operator's own power.**

**(b) A revoked or never-held membership.** `isolated`/`group`: dropped on every request with the warn line, grants re-resolved tenantless; pinned for the revoked member (`u_ex`: `tenantId` undefined, one warn line, the read walled to `RLS_DENY_FILTER` on both conjuncts, the insert refused with the ADR-0123 D2 denial) and for the never-held organization (`org_gamma`: dropped, then the D10 denial). **Unreachable under a wall.** `single`/no posture: kept, as for a session, pinned both ways. **Reachable there exactly as for a browser session, by the ruling's choice of mechanism and documented.**

**(c) The platform-admin global grant.** `derivePosture` reads held capability grants, never the organization; a global `admin_full_access` row applies with or without a tenant. Bound: `posture` `PLATFORM_ADMIN`, read walled to the bound organization on both conjuncts. Unbound: `PLATFORM_ADMIN`, walled to nothing on a business object under `isolated` (ADR-0095 W2), as before. The claim cannot mint `PLATFORM_ADMIN`, and the grant is not widened. **Unchanged; pinned both ways.**

**(d) A token with no claim.** `activeOrganizationId: undefined`, so `tenantId` is undefined and no warn line is written; the card's D10 denial stands. **Today's behaviour; pinned under `isolated` and `single`.**

**(e) The synthetic session trusted without vetting.** The session object is a closure local to `resolveExecutionContext`, consumed only by `resolveAuthzContext`'s session arm; nothing else in the runtime or dispatcher reads it. `ctx.tenantId` is written at `:588` before the vetting at `:712`, and the only exit between them is the unusable-engine branch judged above. The API-key arm pre-empts the session arm entirely, so a key's organization can never be overwritten by the token's. `isSystem` is `false` by construction. The dispatcher's two other organization reads are the cookie session (absent on an OAuth request) and the vetted envelope. **Unreachable.**

**(f) Docs and changeset.** `agents.mdx` states the one-organization rule, the claim name, the wall qualifier on the re-check, the `single` behaviour ("stands as consented, as a session's does"), the empty `200` and refused write under `isolated`, and the pre-binding token's global-only grants until one re-consent. The changeset says the same and names the API-key and session tracks as untouched. Each sentence matches a line of code or a pin read here. **No overstatement found.**

### ③ Pins

The rig runs the REAL `resolveExecutionContext` into the REAL `resolveAuthzContext` (core resolved to source by the package's vitest alias) over a table double, and hands the envelope to the REAL `SecurityPlugin` middleware; only `verifyMcpAccessToken` is faked, and its half is pinned against a real authorization server in PR #24218. Vacuity checks: the `{ posture }` double is read by `effectiveTenancyPosture(tenancy.posture)`, so the posture reaches both the resolver and the wall; `bindCatalogFromTables` makes the catalog the resolver reads real; `droppedClaimLines` matches the exact text `warnSessionOrganizationClaimDropped` prints, principal and organization included; the positive case asserts the real Layer 0 composition (`[{ organization_id: org_alpha }, { organization_id: org_alpha }]`) and an admitted insert, not merely `tenantId`. The ruling's four controls are each present and discriminating (the other-organization control is asserted in both directions, so it excludes the union rather than only the absence of grants). The claim-less token, the non-member organization, the `single` composition and the four-posture token/session parity are pinned. Gaps, both named in the PR body: no middleware-level pin under `group`; no pin for the API-key-beside-JWT composition (pre-existing, out of scope).

**The ablation reading.** 13 of 15 red is sound. Every control except the two claim-less ones opens with the organization it was vetted in (the bound `tenantId`, or the dropped-claim line), and only then asserts the refusal. That ordering is what makes the controls non-vacuous: with the organization removed, "refused at D10" is true for any organization-scoped grant, so a refusal-only control would pass under ablation and prove nothing about the boundary. The two pure negatives (claim-less, `isolated` and `single`) stayed green, which is the template's "controls stay green" expectation applied to the controls it fits. The dev read the direction correctly.

### ④ Flags

1. **Resource `custom_claims` override, out of scope.** Agree. Unreachable from any public door (②a), vetted under a wall by the mechanism the ruling fixes, and under `single` it is a store-level operator's own power. A hardening follow-up belongs to `domain:services` (have the authorization server ignore or refuse `organization_id` arriving from a resource row, or pin the seeded MCP resource row to carry no `custom_claims`), not this PR.
2. **The dropped-claim warn line for a token.** Agree. Core's line, read-only for this slice; it names the principal and the organization, and prints its unknown placeholder for the session id because the synthetic session has no row. Cosmetic; a later core card could carry the token's `azp` on that line. Not a gap.
3. **The stale `[#4127 FINDING, batch 5]` comment.** Agree. Prose on the session getter, outside this slice's surface, no security content.
